query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but its poor oxygen resistance limits practical high-temperature use. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing the alloy’s useful mechanical performance? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention and mechanism, the predicted change relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr, the relevant temperature, atmosphere, exposure time, and mechanical-loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Applying a nanoscale, conformal Al2O3 coating via atomic layer deposition (ALD) on as‐cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr will significantly improve its oxidation resistance at high temperatures (~1000 °C) without adversely affecting its intrinsic room-temperature ductility (8–16%) and high-temperature yield strength (163–530 MPa).
generation.material_initial_state: As‐cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr alloy exhibiting good mechanical performance but poor oxygen resistance.
generation.intervention: Deposit a thin (nanoscale) conformal Al2O3 protective coating using atomic layer deposition (ALD) on the alloy surface.
generation.conditions: Exposure in an oxygen-rich atmosphere at approximately 1000 °C for 100 hours, with concurrent mechanical testing at strain rates between 10−4 and 10−2 s−1.
generation.structural_mediator: The ALD-deposited Al2O3 layer acts as a surface barrier that impedes oxygen diffusion into the alloy.
generation.mechanism: The protective Al2O3 coating reduces oxygen ingress and subsequent oxidation by forming a stable, high-temperature barrier, thereby preserving the underlying alloy's microstructure and its mechanical properties.
generation.predicted_outcome: The coated alloy will show a marked reduction in oxidation (i.e., less formation of oxide scales or oxygen-induced embrittlement) relative to the untreated alloy while maintaining its established ductility and yield strength at high temperatures.
generation.baseline: Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr demonstrates acceptable ductility and yield strength but suffers from rapid oxidation in oxygen-rich, high-temperature environments.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is applicable under conditions of oxygen-rich atmospheres at ~1000 °C, exposure durations up to about 100 hours, and strain rates ranging from 10−4 to 10−2 s−1. Variations beyond these conditions require further validation.
generation.uncertainty: Optimal coating thickness and ALD processing parameters need further investigation to ensure minimal impact on mechanical properties; additional studies are necessary to fine-tune these parameters.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of as‐cast HfNbTaTiZr samples: one set with the nanoscale Al2O3 coating deposited by ALD, and a control set without any coating. Subject both sets to an oxygen-rich atmosphere at ~1000 °C for 100 hours. Following exposure, perform tensile tests at strain rates between 10−4 and 10−2 s−1, and conduct microstructural evaluations (via SEM/TEM and XRD) to assess oxidation depth, oxide layer formation, and any alterations to the mechanical properties.
measurements: Oxidation mass gain and oxide layer thickness by SEM/TEM
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the ALD-coated samples do not exhibit a statistically significant reduction in oxidation (e.g., similar oxide layer thickness or mass gain) compared to the control set, or if there is a measurable deterioration in ductility or yield strength, the hypothesis will be falsified.

cited_evidence.text: The equiatomic HfMoNbTaTiZr alloy was chosen to analyze the effect of each constituent elemental by the subtraction method and, thus, HfMoNbTaTiZr, HfNbTaTiZr, HfMoTaTiZr, HfMoNbTiZr, HfMoNbTaZr, and HfMoNbTaTi were studied. Among these alloys, HfMoNbTaTi has the best mechanical performance, that is, 27% compressive strain at room temperature and yield strength 367 MPa at 1400 °C. HfMoNbTaTi has great potential for elevated-temperature applications. As the alloy system does not contain very expensive elements such as Re and Ru, it is cost competitive for high-temperature applications like Nb-Hf-Ti alloys in space vehicles. Further modification of composition and/or anti-oxidation coatings are still required for high-temperature applications in the air. According to the experiment results, the effects of Mo, Nb, Ta, Ti, and Zr on mechanical properties of equiatomic Hf-Mo-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr alloys were described. For higher room-temperature strength, one should add an element which interacts frequently with the alloy, such as Mo. chosen.lever: surface modification via a thin protective coating
chosen.technique: atomic layer deposition (ALD) of an Al2O3 film

chosen.why: This intervention directly targets the performance limitation by establishing a barrier that impedes oxygen ingress, drawing on prior evidence of improved oxidation resistance via protective oxide coatings.
